questions.q: The page lists two Mars orbiters from 2013: India's Mangalyaan and NASA's MAVEN. How much did each cost?
questions.do: Scroll to Same goal, different price and read the two Mars orbiter rows and the note under the table.
questions.a: Mangalyaan cost $73M and MAVEN $583M. MAVEN cost 8.0 times as much, though it carried different instruments and had a longer prime mission.

questions.q: If every agency puts 10% of its budget into one pool, how many Mangalyaan-class and MAVEN-class missions could it pay for each year?
questions.do: In Pool the money, move Share of each budget put into the pool from 5% to 10%.
questions.a: The joint budget becomes about $5.8 billion a year: about 79 Mangalyaan-class missions or 10 MAVEN-class missions a year (double the 5% figures of $2.9 billion, 39 and 5.0).

questions.q: For a spacecraft where Voyager 2 is in the sky, how much of the day can NASA's dishes alone talk to it, and what changes when everyone shares?
questions.do: In Shared ears: the deep-space dishes, choose NASA and the Voyager 2 position (−58°). Read In contact and Longest silence. Then click Everyone.
questions.a: NASA alone: 76% of each day, with a longest silence of 5.7 hours. Everyone together: 100% of the day, no silence, and two or more dishes at once all day. Dishes spread around the world always keep one in view.

questions.q: Why does a better engine shrink the “mountain” of mass needed in Earth orbit for a crewed Mars trip?
questions.do: In The research levers: people to Mars, set Engine for the trip between planets to ISRO Vikas and untick both levers. Read The mountain of mass in orbit. Then pick NASA NERVA and tick Aerocapture and Make fuel on Mars.
questions.a: Vikas with no tricks needs about 2,348 t in orbit. NERVA with both levers needs about 475 t, 4.9× lighter. NERVA's specific impulse (841 s against 293 s) means each kilogram of fuel gives far more push, and the levers brake in Mars's air and make fuel for the trip home on Mars, so less is carried from Earth.

questions.q: Bringing a sample back through Earth's air has been done by only three agencies. Which first missions does the page name for them?
questions.do: In Assemble a mission from everyone's best, click Bring rock home from Mars and read the step Bring a sample back through Earth's air.
questions.a: NASA: Apollo 11, CNSA: Chang'e 5 and JAXA: Hayabusa. Each is the first mission in which that agency showed it could do this step.
